rule: Derek 2026-10-14 (#6694): a page either auditor calls worse is not written; STOP if Opus calls any worse or Gemini > 4/40

worse.line: B worse (yes/no) (nominal): α −0.03 [−0.08, 0.00], 40 pages — not settled

rows.opus_note: The leaf reads 'Minerӕ' and 'ernehrende'; Y misreads 'Minoræ' and modernizes the spelling ('ihr', 'Ursach', 'ernährende'), but the sense is intact.
rows.gemini_note: Y misreads 'Mineræ' as 'Minoræ' and corrupts 'dem-' into 'dems'.

rows.opus_note: Y drops 'creaturis' from 'nihil creaturis uisibile, ut Fortunatus', which changes the sense, and alters the printed 'Marcellius' to 'Marcellus'.
rows.gemini_note: Y omits 'creaturis' before 'uisibile' and changes 'Marcellius' to 'Marcellus'.

rows.opus_note: X keeps the Hebrew as printed ('קירון עור פנים') and reads 'sit'; Y normalizes the Hebrew to 'קֶרֶן עוֹר פָּנִים' and twice gives 'fit' for 'sit', though Y correctly has the Greek 'ὃς τις'.
rows.gemini_note: Y alters the leaf's printed 'קירון עור פנים' to 'קֶרֶן עוֹר פָּנִים' and inserts an unprinted 'דִּי'.

rows.opus_note: The leaf prints 'otio is ali solet' and 'quibusdam'; X omits 'is' and gives 'quibusdā'. Otherwise the two are near-identical.
rows.gemini_note: Y is more faithful because X omits 'is' from 'otio is ali solet'.

rows.opus_note: The body texts are identical; Y only adds a spurious '<sig>s</sig>' taken from show-through and bolds 'Deum'.
rows.gemini_note: Y correctly transcribes the signature mark ('<sig>s</sig>'), which X omits as show-through.

rows.opus_note: Y matches 'quartæ quintæue partis', 'Conseruæ', 'Enulæ' and 'I. Q.'; X drops the '-ue' ('quartæ quintæ') and gives 'Conferuæ', 'Enula' and 'pleurifibus'.
rows.gemini_note: X misreads 'I. Q.' as 'I. 2.' and omits '-ue' from 'quartæ quintæue partis'.

rows.opus_note: Y collapses the subscript leaf numbers into wrong figures ('24V, 50V' for 'X4v, X5v'; '288 V' for '21₈v'; 'IV 11, 12 & 13'), which misstates the collation.
rows.gemini_note: Y misreads the bibliographical collation notes by flattening subscript leaf numbers into standard digits (e.g., '1₁ - 22₆' as '11 - 226') and garbling 'X₄v, X₅v, 1₁' as '24V, 50V, 41'.

rows.opus_note: The leaf reads 'kulminirt', 'frugi', 'Aukto=rität' and 'funfzigsten'; Y's 'fulminirt' and 'fruggi' are wrong words, and its header reads 'Bom' for 'Vom'.
rows.gemini_note: Y misreads 'kulminirt' as the sense-changing 'fulminirt', alongside errors like 'Bom' for 'Vom' and 'fruggi' for 'frugi'.

rows.opus_note: The leaf reads 'ductore Bor-bonio'; X garbles the name as 'Bo-bonio' and leaves HTML '&' entities. Y is otherwise faithful.
rows.gemini_note: X drops the 'r' at the line break, reading 'Bor-bonio' as 'Bo-bonio'.

rows.opus_note: The leaf reads '曰干扞也…青裘豹褎麛裘青豻褎豹取制服豻取守也'; X has '干豻也', '豹豻裘青豻裘' and '豹取守也', which change the gloss. X's page number '百十一' is also wrong.
rows.gemini_note: X corrupts the entry for 豻, omitting '麛裘' and misreading '扞' as '豻' and '豻取守也' as '豹取守也'.

rows.opus_note: X drops abbreviation marks, giving 'Christianus' for 'Christianū', 'scatet'/'resonat' for 'scatēt'/'resonāt', 'minitate' for 'minitāte' and 'fannis' for 'sannis', where Y reads correctly; the words change but the sense still comes through.
rows.gemini_note: Y correctly expands abbreviation marks and identifies the catchword, whereas X drops macrons producing truncated forms like 'nullu' and appends 'utinam' to the running text.

rows.opus_note: Both carry the full text of both columns, the Hebrew and Greek verse and the marginal numbers; Y has small slips ('creada', 'mudi') and X has 'Qvid', and none of them change the meaning.
rows.gemini_note: X is more faithful to the leaf, whereas Y introduces erroneous readings such as 'creada' for 'creanda' and 'mudi' for 'mūdi'.

rows.opus_note: Y misreads several words in ways that change the meaning: 'ملكية' for 'صلحيّة', 'وجد' for 'وجّه', 'الخزاعي' for 'اليها', 'فاذاروان' for 'همذان فاثروا', 'فنفذه' for 'فخنقه' and 'وبنى بها دارا' for 'وحبس بها'; X matches the print.
rows.gemini_note: Y introduces serious hallucinations, including adding 'الخزاعي' and corrupting 'وحبس بها' to 'وبنى بها دارا'.

rows.opus_note: X misreads 'praxim ītroductorijs' as 'parim īproductorijs', writes 'eorum:dem' for 'eorun-dem', and adds a title heading ('Domini Simphoriani / champerii lugdunensi') that is not printed twice on the page; Y matches the line breaks and readings.
rows.gemini_note: X misreads 'praxim' as 'parim' and 'ītroductorijs' as 'īproductorijs'.

rows.opus_note: Y leaves out 'rem' in 'Non recte rem intellexisse', has 'plebe' for 'plebs' and 'predicta' for 'prodicta', and changes the apparatus variant 'Retulius' to 'Rutilius'; X reads all of these correctly.
rows.gemini_note: Y misreads 'prodicta die' as 'predicta die', omits 'rem', and alters 'Retulius' to 'Rutilius'.

rows.opus_note: Y has 'constit.' for 'consistit', 'Extistit' for 'Existit', margin note '§ διαλυσις' for 'ἢ διαλύονται', and section number '82' where the page prints '62'; X follows the page.
rows.gemini_note: Y misreads the marginal note '* ἢ διαλύονται.' as '§ διαλυσις' and duplicates 'sim' in 'uicissim sim'.

rows.opus_note: X drops 'Lactuca siue endiuia que maioris est amaritudinis' (garbled as 'Ubi gal. Lacus dinis'), has 'spoliata' for 'composita' and 'orizuccaro' for 'oxizuccaro', and gives the signature as 'd ij' where the page has 'M ij'; Y is accurate.
rows.gemini_note: X garbles multiple passages, corrupting 'Ca. clxix.' into 'Ca. chir.' and truncating 'Lactuca siue endiuia que maioris est amaritudinis' into 'Lacus dinis'.

rows.opus_note: The printed title is the same in both, but X calls the medallion portrait Virgil when its legend names Aldus Pius Manutius, and X leaves out the handwritten '3' and the 'R' mark that Y records.
rows.gemini_note: X omits the medallion inscription ('ALDVS PIVS MANVTIVS') and the stamped 'R'.

rows.opus_note: Y is badly garbled: chapters 'Ca. c.' and 'cij' twice where the page has 'cx', 'cxj', 'cxij', 'bonum magnitudine' for 'boum', and the invented 'In africa et ethiopia'; X gives a faithful expanded reading.
rows.gemini_note: Y severely garbles the text throughout, misreading 'Mortuū' as 'Adortum' and corrupting 'adunata em vl lulant' into 'adunata emulant'.

rows.opus_note: Y has 'in stannum verretur' where the page prints 'con-vertetur' and 'excaldescat' where it prints 'excādescat'; otherwise the two are the same.
rows.gemini_note: Y misreads 'convertetur' as 'verretur' by omitting line-end 'con-', and has 'excaldescat' for 'excandescat'.

rows.opus_note: Identical wording; X only normalizes 'vnd' to 'und' where the print has 'vnd Stunde/vnd auff'.
rows.gemini_note: Y faithfully preserves 'vnd' as printed on line 5, whereas X replaces it with 'und'.

rows.opus_note: Text and apparatus match the page in both; Y adds the section numbers 16-19 and X tags '[327]' as gloss, which are markup differences only.
rows.gemini_note: X omits the section numbers 16, 17, 18, and 19 from the main text (e.g., '16 quem casus sedendi fecerat').

rows.opus_note: Y has several sense-changing misreadings, e.g. 'nisi his calamitossimis' for 'nostris', 'Nam quod ea etiam' for 'Nam quis eam quaeso', 'pretium' for 'perpetuum', 'quartum auguror' for 'quantum', and it drops 'cum' before 'crebrioribus'.
rows.gemini_note: Y corrupts multiple words and Latin abbreviations into sense-changing errors, such as reading 'perpetuum' as 'pretium' and 'Nam quis eam quaeso' as 'Nam quod ea etiam'.

rows.opus_note: Y misreads 'pcitatē' ('parcitatem') as 'pecuniam serves', 'impitorum' ('imperitorum') as 'impiorum' and 'rides' as 'rites', and it drops 'de' in 'de tusculanis'.
rows.gemini_note: Y introduces multiple sense-changing errors including 'pecuniam' for 'parcitatem' and 'impiorum' for 'imperitorum'.

rows.opus_note: The leaf is blank and shows only mirrored show-through; Y transcribes that as a title page ('BASILICA CHYMICA ... M. DC. XLVI.'), which invents the date.
rows.gemini_note: Y incorrectly transcribes mirrored show-through from the recto ('BASILICA CHYMICA') on a blank page.

rows.opus_note: X has 'integra' for the printed 'integræ' and leaves 'idē' out of the margin note 'Phædone idē: ne putet'; Y has both, and the other differences are spelling conventions.
rows.gemini_note: X omits 'idē:' in the third marginal note.

rows.opus_note: X gives wrong citations and words: 'Ezech. 29. 7.' for 'Es. 23. v. 7', 'De gloria data' for 'Deo gloria dāda', 'partes confluentes corpus eius Ecclesiam cum Spiritu' for 'constituentes corpus eius Ecclesiasticum & spirituale', and 'Matth. 23. 8. 9.' without the '10'.
rows.gemini_note: X misreads 'partes constituentes corpus eius Ecclesiasticum & spirituale' as 'partes confluentes corpus eius Ecclesiam cum Spiritu' and substitutes 'Ezech. 29. 7.' for 'Es. 23. v. 7.'.

rows.opus_note: Only small spelling differences ('Vrsache'/'Vrsachē', 'liegen'/'ligē', 'ganze'/'gantze'), and Y is slightly closer to the print in each.
rows.gemini_note: Y correctly preserves the printed spellings 'gantze' and 'ligen', whereas X normalizes them to 'ganze' and 'liegen'.

rows.opus_note: X has 'Skiße' in the header (the print reads 'Skizze') and 'Verhältnis' for 'Verhältniß'; neither changes the sense.
rows.gemini_note: Y faithfully preserves the printed Greek diacritics ('οὑτος', 'ὁ', 'γεννᾳ') and historical Fraktur spelling ('Verhältniß'), whereas X omits the diacritics and modernizes the spelling.

rows.opus_note: X gives the month lengths as 'undetvicenum' and 'undetvicenis' (19 days) where the print has 'undetricenum' and 'undetricenis' (29 days), and it drops 'Zeunius' from the note.
rows.gemini_note: X omits the name 'Zeunius' ('Zeunius iubet conferri') in the commentary and misreads 'undetricenum' as 'undetvicenum'.

rows.opus_note: X reads 'Christophorus parisiensis', 'Einem' and 'sogenanten' as printed; Y has 'parifienfis' and normalizes to 'sogennanten'.
rows.gemini_note: X correctly transcribes 'Christophorus parisiensis', 'Einem', and 'sogenanten', whereas Y misreads the long s as 'f' in 'parifienfis' and alters the spelling to 'sogenannten'.

rows.opus_note: X keeps the printed 'hervorbläckende' and lowercase 'den'; Y normalizes to 'hervorbleckende' and has 'Den'.
rows.gemini_note: X misreads 'hervorbleckende' as 'hervorbläckende' and lowercases initial 'Den'.

rows.opus_note: X has the printed 'næ vitæ', 'Physicæ' and 'præhenfionem'; Y has 'ne', 'Physica' and 'prahenfionem'.
rows.gemini_note: Y misreads the 'æ' ligature in 'næ' as 'ne', 'Physicæ' as 'Physica', and 'præhenſionem' as 'prahenfionem'.

rows.opus_note: The only difference is that Y keeps the printed misspelling 'incoporata' and X normalizes it to 'incorporata'.
rows.gemini_note: The leaf prints 'incoporata' in line 1, which Y faithfully retains while X silently corrects to 'incorporata'.

rows.opus_note: X matches '以足至者也' and '故牝曰麐也'; Y invents '以足以至', garbles the end as '故從君麇也' and uses the wrong character 麇 throughout.
rows.gemini_note: Y misidentifies the subject 麐 as '麇' and invents '故從君麇也' where the leaf reads '故牝曰麐也'.

rows.opus_note: Y misreads 'asianus' as 'alianus', 'antequam' as 'antea' and 'tibique pro pena' as 'tibi quod per pena'; X is accurate apart from normalizing 'vitens' to 'videns'.
rows.gemini_note: Y corrupts 'tibique pro pena' into 'tibi quod per pena' and misreads 'videns' as 'vitens'.

rows.opus_note: Y has the printed 'promovit' and 'eâdem'; X has 'promovet'.
rows.gemini_note: X misreads 'promovit' as 'promovet', gives 'Magia illicita' for 'Magiæ illicitæ' in the margins, and erroneously appends the catchword 'funde-' to the body text.

rows.opus_note: The texts are identical except for 'CAP.' vs the printed 'CAPVT' and 'vitae' vs 'uitae'.
rows.gemini_note: Both transcriptions are equally faithful to the leaf; minor differences in header abbreviation ('CAP.' vs 'CAPVT') and orthography ('vitae' vs 'uitae') are conventions that do not matter to a reader.

rows.opus_note: Y reads the printed 'iudicamus' correctly; X has 'indicamus'.
rows.gemini_note: Y has 'iudicamus' where the leaf reads 'indicamus'.

rows.opus_note: The wording is identical; they differ only in how they render the apothecary sign (X '$\mathfrak{z}$', Y a mix of '℥' and 'ʒ').
rows.gemini_note: X misreads the apothecary ounce symbol as 'ξ' and as drachm '$\mathfrak{z}$' in 'cassiæ pro clystere', altering medical quantities.
